# PR preview environment on RWX: https://www.rwx.com/blog/preview-your-web-apps-with-rwx
# Serves the exported frontend and Reflex backend through Caddy on port 3000,
# mirroring the Dockerfile/entrypoint.sh production layout.
on:
  github:
    pull_request:
      init:
        commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}
        pull-request-number: ${{ event.github.pull_request.number }}
  cli:
    init:
      commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}

base:
  image: ubuntu:24.04
  config: rwx/base 1.2.0

# The code, uv-install, deps and reflex-export tasks are byte-identical to
# reflex-build.yml so RWX's content cache reuses its result instead of
# re-running the export; keep them in lockstep.
tasks:
  - key: code
    call: git/clone 2.2.0
    with:
      repository: https://github.com/elviskahoro/reflex-starter-template.git
      ref: ${{ init.commit-sha }}
      fetch-full-depth: true
      preserve-git-dir: true

  - key: uv-install
    run: |
      set -euo pipefail
      script="$(mktemp)"
      trap 'rm -f "${script}"' EXIT
      curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/0.11.13/install.sh -o "${script}"
      echo "48cd5aca5d5671a3b3d5f61538cc8622e4434af63319115159990d8b0dd02416  ${script}" | sha256sum -c -
      sh "${script}"
      echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> $RWX_ENV/PATH

  - key: deps
    use: [code, uv-install]
    filter:
      - pyproject.toml
      - uv.lock
    run: |
      uv sync --frozen
      echo "$PWD/.venv/bin" >> $RWX_ENV/PATH
      echo "VIRTUAL_ENV=$PWD/.venv" >> $RWX_ENV/VIRTUAL_ENV

  - key: reflex-export
    use: [code, deps]
    run: |
      uv run reflex init
      uv run reflex export --frontend-only
    env:
      REFLEX_ENV: prod
      PYTHONUNBUFFERED: "1"

  - key: system-deps
    run: |
      sudo apt-get update
      sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends caddy unzip

  - key: build
    use: [reflex-export, system-deps]
    run: |
      sudo mkdir -p /srv
      sudo unzip -q frontend.zip -d /srv
      rm frontend.zip
      # The export bakes in http://localhost:8000; point it at the page origin
      # instead (Caddy proxies /_event and /_upload to the backend).
      f=$(grep -rl 'localhost:8000' /srv/assets | head -1)
      printf '%s\n' \
        'const o=location.origin,w=o.replace(/^http/,"ws");' \
        'var e={PING:o+"/ping",EVENT:w+"/_event",UPLOAD:o+"/_upload",AUTH_CODESPACE:o+"/auth-codespace",HEALTH:o+"/_health",ALL_ROUTES:o+"/_all_routes",TRANSPORT:"websocket",TEST_MODE:!1};export{e as t};' \
        | sudo tee "$f" > /dev/null

  - key: preview
    use: [build]
    app:
      endpoint: pr-${{ init.pull-request-number }}
      port: 3000
    run: |
      export PORT=3000 REFLEX_ENV=prod
      .venv/bin/reflex run --env prod --backend-only --backend-port 8000 &
      exec caddy run --config Caddyfile --adapter caddyfile

  - key: share-link
    use: [preview]
    run: echo "$PREVIEW_URL"
    env:
      PREVIEW_URL: ${{ tasks.preview.app.url }}

**https://pr-0--elviskahoro.rwx.run/rwx-share?code=m3mZ4c5_yEr4aI5mrsT1vg**

The link is valid for 7 days. The preview is private, so you need this link to open it.

- **How I deployed it:** I ran `.rwx/preview.yml` with `pull-request-number=0`, which gives the endpoint `pr-0`. The run succeeded, and I made the link with `rwx apps share pr-0`. The run is at https://cloud.rwx.com/elviskahoro/runs/01a1bec2489a74a2a1b075d4287bec9b.
- **What was deployed:** The pipeline clones the remote repo at the commit SHA instead of using local files. So the preview shows the pushed commit, not unpushed local changes. The working tree is clean, so there's nothing local that it would miss.

To turn the preview off, run `rwx apps disable pr-0`.

# `rwx sandbox background restart`

Sync local changes and restart a managed background process.

## Usage

```
rwx sandbox background restart [config-file] --key <key> [flags]

```

## Description

Sync local changes to the sandbox, stop the process, and start its original command again. A process started with `rwx sandbox background --port` keeps its sandbox port and reuses its local port if available. If that local port is in use, the CLI allocates a new one and prints the updated preview URL.

You can also restart a process declared in the sandbox task's [background-processes](/docs/background-processes) by its configured key. If you exposed it separately with [rwx sandbox tunnel](/docs/cli-reference/rwx-sandbox/tunnel), run that command again after restarting to reopen the tunnel.

Use this when an application needs a hard restart to pick up changes. If a restart isn't needed, [rwx sandbox exec](/docs/cli-reference/rwx-sandbox/exec) syncs changes and runs a command, while [rwx sandbox push](/docs/cli-reference/rwx-sandbox/push) syncs them without running one.

To change the command or its port, use [rwx sandbox background](/docs/cli-reference/rwx-sandbox/background) with the same key instead.

Every file has an `on.cli` trigger, so all can be started locally.

## Run a pipeline with local changes

`rwx run` sends a git patch; no commit or push needed for the changes themselves:

- Base: closest ancestor of local `HEAD` already on `origin` (`event.git.sha`) — resolves even when the branch itself was never pushed. Resolution fails only when the branch shares no commits with `origin` (or no remote is configured); the error surfaces when the run starts, not at clone — push once in that case.
- Patch: unpushed commits, staged, unstaged and untracked files. `.gitignore`d files are excluded; Git LFS changes error out (documented in `rwx run --help`).
- `RWX_DISABLE_GIT_PATCH=1` (any non-empty value) disables patching; `RWX_GIT_REMOTE` changes the remote it patches against (default `origin`). See `rwx docs pull /docs/cli-reference/environment-variables`.

```bash
rwx run .rwx/tests.yml --wait --fail-fast
rwx run .rwx/tests.yml --target <task-key> --wait     # one task plus dependencies
rwx run .rwx/pyright.yml --wait --init paths="web/foo.py web/bar.py"
rwx run .rwx/pyrefly.yml --wait
rwx run .rwx/tests.yml --title "wip: my change" --json
```

Keep `commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}` in the `cli` trigger and `ref: ${{ init.commit-sha }}` on `git/clone`; that wiring makes the patch apply. Use pyright/pyrefly runs when there is no local `.venv` or memory is tight.

## Results, logs, artifacts

```bash
rwx runs list
rwx results <run-id>                              # status and failures (also: rwx results -h for branch/commit lookup)
rwx logs <task-id>
rwx logs <run-id> --task <task-key> --output /tmp/logs
rwx artifacts --help
rwx retry --help ; rwx cancel --help ; rwx debug --help ; rwx ssh --help
```
---
name: rwx-reflex-preview
description: Set up, run, debug, and access RWX preview apps (.rwx/preview.yml) for this Reflex starter. Use when working on PR previews, `rwx run`, rwx.run URLs, or preview auth.
---

# RWX preview apps for Reflex

Config lives in `.rwx/preview.yml`. Docs: https://www.rwx.com/docs/apps and
https://www.rwx.com/blog/preview-your-web-apps-with-rwx. Stick to the docs and
`rwx <cmd> --help`; don't guess at syntax.

## Layout

Tasks: `code` (git/clone) -> `uv-install` (checksum-pinned uv) -> `deps`
(`uv sync --frozen`) -> `reflex-export` (`reflex export --frontend-only`)
-> `system-deps` (caddy, unzip) -> `build` (unzips `frontend.zip` to
`/srv`) -> `preview` (`app:` task, port 3000, runs backend on :8000 +
Caddy via the repo Caddyfile) -> `share-link` (prints
`tasks.preview.app.url`).

`code`/`uv-install`/`deps`/`reflex-export` are byte-identical to
`reflex-build.yml` so RWX's content cache reuses its export instead of
re-running it; keep them in lockstep.

## Commands

- Validate: `rwx lint .rwx/preview.yml` (also flags outdated package versions)
- Test: `rwx run .rwx/preview.yml --init pull-request-number=0 --wait`
  (a local run has no PR number, so `init.pull-request-number` must be passed)
- Logs: `rwx logs <run-id> --task <key> --output <dir>`; app URL is in the
  `share-link` task log.
- `rwx apps enable|disable <endpoint-or-url>`; `rwx runs list|show`.

## Gotchas learned

- `entrypoint.sh` hardcodes `/app/Caddyfile`; on RWX run the backend and
  `caddy run --config Caddyfile` directly with `PORT=3000`.
- Apps are private by default. Per the docs: set `app.public: true`, use
  `rwx apps share`, or send `X-RWX-Access-Token: $RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN`
  (needs `run:read`). Unauthenticated requests get a 302 to cloud.rwx.com.
- The exported frontend bakes in `http://localhost:8000` (see
  `assets/reflex-env-*.js`), so events fail ("Connection Error") on a preview.
  The current `build` task rewrites that file to use `location.origin`. This is
  NOT documented by RWX or Reflex and an event/WebSocket round trip is still
  unverified; prefer a documented fix (`api_url` / `REFLEX_API_URL` at export)
  if the preview URL can be known at build time.
- Verified: `/` returns 200 and `/ping` returns `pong` with the token header.

---
name: rwx
description: Use when working with RWX: creating or modifying a `.rwx/` run definition, validating a change against remote CI with the RWX CLI (rwx run --wait, rwx results, rwx logs, rwx artifacts) so a pull request has a passing build before review, checking why CI is red or what is failing on a branch, or running tests in an RWX sandbox, or authenticating the RWX CLI (access tokens, `rwx whoami`, which workspace a token belongs to).
---

# RWX: pull requests from agents with passing builds

Sources: the [rwx-cloud/skills](https://github.com/rwx-cloud/skills) `rwx` skill (MIT, v0.2.0), [Truly continuous integration](https://www.rwx.com/blog/ensuring-pull-requests-from-agents-have-passing-builds) (Jordan Sanders, 2026-01-21). Requires RWX CLI 3.0.0 or newer. See also [RWX logs](https://www.rwx.com/blog/rwx-logs) (Jason Robinaugh, 2026-01-07) and [Build container images](https://www.rwx.com/docs/guides/build-container-images), [RWX Sandboxes](https://www.rwx.com/blog/rwx-sandboxes), and the [calculator-demo `claude.yml`](https://github.com/rwx-cloud/calculator-demo/blob/main/.rwx/claude.yml).

Reviewers don't want agent PRs without a green build, and agents often can't run the full suite locally. RWX lets the agent iterate against remote, parallelized CI until it passes, with no commit or push per attempt.

## Authentication

The CLI reads a token from, in order: `--access-token`, `$RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN`, then `~/.config/rwx/accesstoken` (what `rwx login` writes). Check which one is active, and who it is:

```bash
rwx whoami          # token kind, organization, user
```

In Conductor cloud workspaces the startup script validates `RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN` and persists it to `~/.config/rwx/accesstoken` (see [`conductor-startup-script`](../conductor-startup-script/SKILL.md)). If `rwx whoami` fails, run `rwx login` in a terminal or set `RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN` in the workspace's environment variables and re-run setup.

### One token per RWX workspace

Env vars named `RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN_<SUFFIX>` or `RWC_ACCESS_TOKEN_<SUFFIX>` may also be injected, each scoped to one RWX organization (`<SUFFIX>` is the uppercased org/owner name). The CLI doesn't read these names, so export the right one under `RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN`. List names without values:

```bash
env | grep -E '^RW[XC]_ACCESS_TOKEN_.' | cut -d= -f1
```

Pick the token whose suffix matches the repo owner. `export` lasts for the whole shell session, so re-run this (or `unset RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN`) when you switch repos or organizations:

```bash
OWNER=$(git remote get-url origin | sed -E 's#.*[:/]([^/]+)/[^/]+(\.git)?$#\1#' | tr a-z A-Z)
TOKEN="$(printenv "RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN_$OWNER" || printenv "RWC_ACCESS_TOKEN_$OWNER")"
[ -n "$TOKEN" ] && export RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN="$TOKEN"   # an empty export would shadow ~/.config/rwx/accesstoken
rwx whoami
```

A run, task, or log ID only resolves under the organization that owns it. On not-found or unauthorized, switch tokens. Never print, log, or commit a token value.

## Writing and validating run definitions

Don't write `.rwx/*.yml` from memory. Pull the reference and read all of it without truncating:

```bash
rwx docs pull /migrating/rwx-reference
rwx docs search "<query>"          # for anything the reference doesn't cover, then rwx docs pull the hit
rwx lint .rwx/<name>.yml           # validate before running
```

`rwx run` doesn't need a commit or push, even when the definition references a commit SHA: RWX patches the git clone with your local contents.

## Running CI on your working tree

`rwx run` sends a git patch with the run, so no commit or push is needed:

- Base: the closest ancestor of local `HEAD` that is already on `origin`. `event.git.sha` resolves to it.
- Patch on top: unpushed commits, staged and unstaged changes, untracked files. Anything in `.gitignore` is excluded. Git LFS changes error out; commit and push those first.
- `RWX_DISABLE_GIT_PATCH=1` turns patching off.

```bash
rwx run .rwx/ci.yml --wait --fail-fast             # run on the working tree, stop at first failure
rwx run .rwx/ci.yml --target <task-key> --wait     # one task and its dependencies (repeatable)
rwx run .rwx/ci.yml --init key=value --title "wip" # init params, run title
```

For the patch to apply, `git/clone` takes `ref: ${{ init.commit-sha }}` and the `cli` trigger sets `commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}`. A cli-dispatched run starts with an empty workspace, so the definition must clone the repo itself (see the header of `.rwx/gtm-903-consume-published-image.yml`). Edits to `.rwx` files are picked up locally.

## Checking CI status

To see what is failing on the current or a given branch, start with `rwx results -h`, then `rwx logs` for the failing task.

## Migrating from GitHub Actions

Use the [`migrate-from-gha`](../migrate-from-gha/SKILL.md) skill, then [`review-gha-migration`](../review-gha-migration/SKILL.md).

## Commands

- `rwx run --wait` starts a run and blocks until it finishes. Use it as the agent's validation step.
- `rwx results [run-id]` shows what happened in a run; with no ID it uses the current branch (`--branch`, `--commit`, `--repo`, `--wait`).
- `rwx runs list` lists runs (`--mine`, `--branch`, `--result-status failed`, `--limit`).
- `rwx logs <task-id>` or `rwx logs <run-id> --task <key> --output DIR` downloads task logs.
- `rwx lint .rwx/<name>.yml` validates a run definition (`--fix` applies available fixes). Run it after every edit to `.rwx/*.yml`.
- `rwx docs search "<query>"` / `rwx docs pull <path>` read the docs. Use Bash for these, not WebFetch.
- `rwx artifacts list|download` fetches artifacts a run produced.
- Most commands accept `--format json` for programmatic parsing (`--json` is a shorthand); on `rwx logs`, `--output` is a download path, not a format. Confirm with `rwx <command> --help`.

## Loop

1. Make a change; `rwx lint` any edited `.rwx/*.yml`.
2. `rwx run --wait` (add `--format json` if parsing).
3. On failure, use `rwx results`, then `rwx logs` / `rwx artifacts` for the failing task, fix, and go to 2.
4. Open the PR only once the run is green.

## Sandboxes (inner loop)

RWX sandboxes are persistent cloud environments built from the same run definitions as CI. The agent stays local (your config, tools, oversight) while execution is offloaded. Local changes sync up before each command and back down after. Content-based caching snapshots automatically, so there are no Docker/OCI images to maintain. Each agent gets its own sandbox, so parallel agents and git worktrees don't need per-worktree local setup. They also work when the agent runs somewhere without a dev environment (e.g. Claude Code on the web).

```bash
rwx sandbox init                  # creates .rwx/sandbox.yml from a starter template
rwx sandbox exec -- npm test      # run a command; the sandbox persists between calls
rwx run .rwx/ci.yml --wait        # outer loop: full CI
```

`.rwx/sandbox.yml` in the article's example (`rwx-cloud/sandbox-example`): `on.cli.init.commit-sha` set from `${{ event.git.sha }}`; base `ubuntu:24.04` with `rwx/base` 1.0.3; a `code` task calling `git/clone` (`preserve-git-dir: true`, `repository`, `ref: ${{ init.commit-sha }}`, `github-token: ${{ github.token }}`); and a `sandbox` task that uses `code` and runs `rwx-sandbox`. Customize it for your project, and make sure repo access is configured.

Agent workflow: iterate with `rwx sandbox exec -- <targeted tests>`, then confirm with `rwx run .rwx/ci.yml --wait` before pushing or opening a PR. Installing the [RWX skill](https://www.rwx.com/docs/ai) teaches agents to do this, or instruct it explicitly. The "seconds to start" claim is the vendor's own, and sync timing is worth testing in your workflow.

## Pulling full logs

Test results are semantic output in the RWX UI, and the RWX MCP server surfaces failed tests to agents. Use full logs when you need stack traces or print/trace output.

- `rwx logs <taskId>` downloads a task's logs (CLI 2.3.0+). Take the task ID from the RWX UI URL.
- Choose a download location the agent can read. Check the CLI reference for the flags; the article names only `--json` and `--auto-extract`.
- Example, listing downloaded log files that contain `ERROR`:

```bash
rwx logs <taskId> --auto-extract --json | jq -r '.outputFiles[]' | xargs grep -l "ERROR"
```

- Don't paste whole logs into the prompt. Thousands of lines bloat context, so grep or filter the files instead.
- The MCP server's failed-task output tells agents how to download logs via the CLI. Treat the CLI as a complement to MCP, not a replacement.

## Building container images

RWX builds OCI images natively (`docker build` also works on RWX). Full YAML lives in the `rwx-cloud/rwx-image-example` repo; this is the shape.

- An `image` task configures the image by writing to `$RWX_IMAGE/`: `command`, `user`, and so on.
  ```bash
  echo "$PWD/script.sh" | tee $RWX_IMAGE/command
  ```
- Push with `rwx image push <task-id> --to <remote-tag>`, where the task ID is the `image` task's. Other commands: `rwx image build` (build and pull locally), `rwx image pull`.
- Node.js example: a base like `node:24.11.0-trixie-slim` with `config: none`, then tasks `system` (apt packages, including `curl` and `jq` for `git/clone`), `code` (`git/clone` at the commit SHA), `npm-install` (`npm ci --omit=dev`), and `image`.
  - No `COPY` step. Start with all files and filter per command: `npm-install` filters on `package.json` and `package-lock.json`, so it stays cached until they change.
  - In `image`, set `$RWX_IMAGE/user` to `node` (don't run as root), `$RWX_IMAGE/command` to `node server.js`, and `NODE_ENV=production`.
- Keep build, push and test as separate embedded runs under one orchestrating run. The push run (base `rwx/base`, with `aws/install-cli`, `rwx/install-cli`, `aws/assume-role`) takes the image task ID from `tasks.build-image.tasks.image.id` and the commit SHA as the tag. This keeps push tooling and credentials out of the image. The test run pulls the image, then runs it with `docker: true`, a health check and `rwx-docker-ready-check` before the test command.
- Locked vaults: tasks don't receive the token that started the run. To push such an image, create a service account with `image:access` and `vault:unlock` for each vault used, attach it to a vault the push task can access, and set `RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN` in the push task's env.
- Account IDs, role ARN, region and registry host in the example are placeholders. Replace them.
- The guide's prose and snippet disagree on the Docker preserve option (`preserve-true` vs `preserve-data`). Check the Docker docs before using it.
- Dockerfile syntax is covered in RWX's "Migrating from Dockerfile" docs.

## Running Claude Code on RWX to open a PR

`rwx-cloud/calculator-demo` has `.rwx/claude.yml`, a run that executes Claude Code headlessly and opens a PR from the result. Shape:

- `code`: `git/clone` with `preserve-git-dir: true` so the agent can use git.
- `node`: install via `nodejs/install`, with the version from `rwx/tool-versions` reading `.tool-versions`. `node-modules`: `npm ci`, filtered on `package.json` and `package-lock.json`.
- `claude-code`: `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code`, then write `~/.claude/settings.json` (`permissions.defaultMode: bypassPermissions`) and `~/.claude.json` (`bypassPermissionsModeAccepted`, `hasCompletedOnboarding`), and set config with `claude config set -g` (autoUpdates off, notifications off, verbose).
- `claude`: `cache: false`, `timeout: 30m`. It runs `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions --append-system-prompt "Provide final result output as a pull request description." -p "$prompt"`, then `claude --continue -p` to generate a PR title. Outputs go to `$RWX_VALUES/` (`claude-result`, `pr-title`, `pr-description`), and the description includes `$RWX_RUN_URL` and the prompt. Env: `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC: 1`, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` from a vault secret, `PROMPT_FILE: ${{ run.dir }}/prompt.md`.
- `create-pull-request`: `github/create-pull-request` with a GitHub app token, `branch-prefix: claude/${{ run.id }}`, and title and body from `tasks.claude.values`.

Bypassing permissions is only reasonable because RWX tasks are sandboxed. Keep the OAuth token in a vault, never in the repo. Pin package versions as the demo does (versions above are the demo's; check for newer).

Full file:

```yaml
base:
  os: ubuntu 24.04
  tag: 1.2

tasks:
  - key: code
    call: git/clone 1.9.5
    with:
      repository: https://github.com/rwx-cloud/calculator-demo.git
      ref: main
      preserve-git-dir: true

  - key: tool-versions
    use: code
    call: rwx/tool-versions 1.0.6
    filter: [.tool-versions]

  - key: node
    call: nodejs/install 1.1.11
    with:
      node-version: ${{ tasks.tool-versions.values.nodejs }}

  - key: node-modules
    use: [node, code]
    run: npm ci
    filter:
      - package.json
      - package-lock.json

  - key: claude-code
    use: node
    run: |
      npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code

      mkdir -p ~/.claude
      cat <<'EOF' > ~/.claude/settings.json
      {
        "permissions": {
          "defaultMode": "bypassPermissions"
        }
      }
      EOF

      cat <<'EOF' > ~/.claude.json
      {
        "bypassPermissionsModeAccepted": true,
        "hasCompletedOnboarding": true
      }
      EOF

      claude config set -g autoUpdates false
      claude config set -g preferredNotifChannel notifications_disabled
      claude config set -g theme dark
      claude config set -g verbose true

  - key: gh
    call: github/install-cli 1.0.8

  - key: claude
    use: [gh, claude-code, code]
    cache: false
    timeout: 30m
    run: |
      echo "Running Claude Code..."

      prompt=$(cat $PROMPT_FILE)
      echo "$prompt"

      echo "Executing prompt..."
      claude --dangerously-skip-permissions \
        --append-system-prompt "Provide final result output as a pull request description." \
        -p "$prompt" | tee "$RWX_VALUES/claude-result"

      echo "Generating title..."
      claude --continue --dangerously-skip-permissions \
        -p "Generate a single line summary of the changes that you just made suitable for a pull request title" | tee "$RWX_VALUES/pr-title"

      echo -e "## Run\n" | tee -a "$RWX_VALUES/pr-description"
      echo -e "$RWX_RUN_URL\n\n" | tee -a "$RWX_VALUES/pr-description"

      echo -e "## Prompt\n" | tee -a "$RWX_VALUES/pr-description"
      echo "$prompt" | tee -a "$RWX_VALUES/pr-description"

      echo -e "\n## Result\n" | tee -a "$RWX_VALUES/pr-description"
      cat "$RWX_VALUES/claude-result" | tee -a "$RWX_VALUES/pr-description"
    env:
      CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC: 1
      CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN: ${{ vaults.doug_test.secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
      PROMPT_FILE: ${{ run.dir }}/prompt.md

  - key: create-pull-request
    call: github/create-pull-request 1.0.3
    use: claude
    with:
      github-token: ${{ github-apps.rwx-cloud-bot.token }}
      branch-prefix: claude/${{ run.id }}
      pull-request-title: ${{ tasks.claude.values.pr-title }}
      pull-request-body: ${{ tasks.claude.values.pr-description }}
```

## Why this works

- DAG-based execution and content-based caching keep reruns fast.
- CI runs without a git push/pull and without building container images, so changes validate immediately.
- Tasks are sandboxed with explicit dependencies, so an agent running locally or in the cloud needs no secrets and no up-to-date local dev environment.

The article gives no config snippets. For `.rwx/` run definitions use `rwx docs pull` (above), and confirm flags with `rwx --help` and `rwx run --help`.

# Using RWX

Ensure the user is signed in and on the latest version of the RWX CLI before
getting started: `rwx whoami`

## RWX Run Definition Syntax

When working with RWX, it is extremely important to use the reference
documentation. Run the following command to pull the reference documentation.
The output is already constrained in size, and it is very important to not
truncate the output of this command.

`rwx docs pull /migrating/rwx-reference`

If you encounter a question not covered by these references, use
`rwx docs search "<query>"` to find the relevant documentation page, then
`rwx docs pull` the result.

## Executing Runs

If the user chooses, you can kick off an actual run on RWX:

`rwx run .rwx/<file>.yml --wait`

When the run finishes, results will be shown, and you can iterate until the run
passes.

You do not need to commit or push to invoke a run with RWX, even if the run
definition references a commit sha. RWX will automatically patch the git clone
with the local contents.

## Check CI / run results or status of a branch

If you have been asked to check on run failures or CI failures, or if you have
been asked to check the current run status of the current branch or a given
branch:

`rwx results -h`

## Sandboxes

If the user mentions using a sandbox:

`rwx sandbox exec -- <command>`

## Generate or Modify RWX Config

You may have been tasked with creating, modifying, or understanding/explaining
an RWX CI/CD config for this project. Use the same aforementioned documentation.

When making changes, you can run validation on the config:

    rwx lint .rwx/<name>.yml

# RWX CLI in this repo

Check the CLI first: `rwx --version` and `rwx whoami`. For previews (`.rwx/preview.yml`) also see the `rwx-reflex-preview` skill.

## Auth: injected tokens, one per RWX workspace

Env vars `RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN_<WORKSPACE>` or `RWC_ACCESS_TOKEN_<WORKSPACE>` are injected, each scoped to one RWX workspace. List names only, never values:

```bash
env | grep -E '^RW[XC]_ACCESS_TOKEN_' | cut -d= -f1
```

The CLI reads only `RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN` (or `--access-token`). Export the token whose suffix matches the repo owner (uppercased owner from `git remote`, here `ELVISKAHORO`). Never print it:

```bash
OWNER=$(git remote get-url origin | sed -E 's#.*[:/]([^/]+)/[^/]+(\.git)?$#\1#' | tr a-z A-Z)
export RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN="REDACTED"RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN_$OWNER" || printenv "RWC_ACCESS_TOKEN_$OWNER")"
rwx whoami   # confirm organization
```

Run IDs, task IDs and logs resolve only under the workspace that owns them. If a lookup returns not-found or unauthorized, try the other workspace's token. On a laptop, `rwx login` works instead.

Every file has an `on.cli` trigger, so all can be started locally.

## Run a pipeline with local changes

`rwx run` sends a git patch; no commit or push needed for the changes themselves:

- Base: closest ancestor of local `HEAD` already on `origin` (`event.git.sha`) — resolves even when the branch itself was never pushed. Resolution fails only when the branch shares no commits with `origin` (or no remote is configured); the error surfaces when the run starts, not at clone — push once in that case.
- Patch: unpushed commits, staged, unstaged and untracked files. `.gitignore`d files are excluded; Git LFS changes error out (documented in `rwx run --help`).
- `RWX_DISABLE_GIT_PATCH=1` (any non-empty value) disables patching; `RWX_GIT_REMOTE` changes the remote it patches against (default `origin`). See `rwx docs pull /docs/cli-reference/environment-variables`.

```bash
rwx run .rwx/tests.yml --wait --fail-fast
rwx run .rwx/tests.yml --target <task-key> --wait     # one task plus dependencies
rwx run .rwx/pyright.yml --wait --init paths="web/foo.py web/bar.py"
rwx run .rwx/pyrefly.yml --wait
rwx run .rwx/tests.yml --title "wip: my change" --json
```

Keep `commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}` in the `cli` trigger and `ref: ${{ init.commit-sha }}` on `git/clone`; that wiring makes the patch apply. Use pyright/pyrefly runs when there is no local `.venv` or memory is tight.

## Results, logs, artifacts

```bash
rwx runs list
rwx results <run-id>                              # status and failures (also: rwx results -h for branch/commit lookup)
rwx logs <task-id>
rwx logs <run-id> --task <task-key> --output /tmp/logs
rwx artifacts --help
rwx retry --help ; rwx cancel --help ; rwx debug --help ; rwx ssh --help
```

`rwx run` prints the run URL and ID; `--json` for parsing. A green run is not proof a step worked: read logs for steps that talk to third parties. "CI is red" means: `rwx results` for the branch, then `rwx logs` for the failing task.

## Other commands

- Sandboxes: `rwx sandbox exec -- <command>` (also `init`, `list`, `start`, `stop`, `reset`).
- Preview apps: `rwx apps --help`. Secrets and vars: `rwx vaults --help`. Crons: `rwx crons --help`. Dispatch workflows: `rwx dispatch --help`.
- Package/base-image versions: `rwx resolve`, `rwx update`.

## Create or modify configs

1. Pull the reference in full, without truncating: `rwx docs pull /migrating/rwx-reference`.
2. For anything else: `rwx docs search "<query>"`, then `rwx docs pull <path>` (e.g. `/docs/cli-triggers`, `/docs/cli-reference/rwx-run`). Use these, not WebFetch.
3. Edit, then validate: `rwx lint .rwx/<name>.yml`.
4. Prefer RWX packages, DAG parallelism and content-based caching.
5. Migrating GitHub Actions: upstream skills at https://github.com/rwx-cloud/skills (`migrate-from-gha`, `review-gha-migration`).

Only rely on behavior documented in RWX docs or `rwx --help`.

## Sandboxes (inner loop)

Persistent cloud environments built from run definitions; local changes sync up before each command and back after. Iterate with `rwx sandbox exec -- <targeted tests>`, then confirm with a full `rwx run ... --wait`. Create `.rwx/sandbox.yml` with `rwx sandbox init`.

## Full logs

Use `rwx logs <task-id> --auto-extract --json` and grep the downloaded files (e.g. for `ERROR`) rather than pasting logs into context.

## Container images

`image` tasks write config to `$RWX_IMAGE/` (`command`, `user`); push with `rwx image push <task-id> --to <tag>`. Keep push credentials out of the image by pushing from a separate run. See `rwx docs search "build container images"`.

'''
